what_its_for: Dicloxacillin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections caused by certain staph (Staphylococcus) bacteria. It is commonly used for skin and soft tissue infections, bone infections, and pneumonia caused by bacteria that are resistant to regular penicillin.
how_to_take: Take dicloxacillin by mouth on an EMPTY stomach — at least 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE a meal, or at least 2 to 3 hours AFTER a meal. Food can prevent this medicine from working properly. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take every dose at evenly spaced times throughout the day (for example, every 6 hours) to keep the right amount of medicine in your body. Always finish the full course of treatment even if you feel better, so the infection does not come back.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken every 6 hours (4 times a day). For more serious infections, your doctor may prescribe up to 1,000 mg every 6 hours. The dose for children is based on their weight and will be determined by their doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at the regular time. Do NOT double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store dicloxacillin capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If your pharmacist prepared a liquid form of this medicine, store it in the refrigerator and throw away any unused liquid after 14 days.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking dicloxacillin with food, milk, or fruit juice, as these can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking antibiotics, as it may increase side effects and slow your recovery. Do not take antacids, vitamins, or supplements at the same time without checking with your pharmacist first. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), since dicloxacillin can affect how they work.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; trouble breathing or swallowing (signs of a serious allergic reaction); severe diarrhea, stomach cramps, or bloody stools (which may be a sign of a serious intestinal infection called C. diff); yellowing of the skin or eyes; dark urine or unusual tiredness (possible liver problems); or if your infection does not seem to be getting better after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting dicloxacillin. However, it is very important to keep taking ALL doses until you finish the full prescription, even if you feel completely better. Stopping too early can allow the bacteria to grow back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Dicloxacillin is generally considered safe during pregnancy, but always tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Small amounts may pass into breast milk; talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose is based on weight. Kidney or Liver Disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Penicillin Allergy: Do NOT take dicloxacillin if you are allergic to penicillin, amoxicillin, or any other penicillin-type antibiotic. Also tell your doctor if you have ever had a reaction to cephalosporin antibiotics.
